teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan from suspected heatstroke
teams.body: Fijian rugby is mourning back-row forward Saimoni Vunilagi, who passed away on Friday 7 August in Japan. The 26-year-old was hospitalised with symptoms consistent with severe heatstroke after a training session with his second-division club, Kyushu KV, on Monday 3 August. Temperatures in Fukuoka reached 35 degrees Celsius during the practice. The 196-centimetre forward, who began his professional career in 2023, was highly regarded by his club, who expressed devastation at the sudden loss.

lead.why: The tragic passing of a Fijian professional player is the most critical and high-salience news item in today's coverage.

teams.heading: RFU postpones start of England community rugby season over drought
teams.body: The Rugby Football Union has postponed the start of England's community rugby season by at least two weeks due to widespread drought conditions. With 71.3% of the country currently in a drought after its driest July since 1836, many pitches are unsafe for contact play. Originally scheduled to begin on the fifth of September, opening fixtures have been pushed back to the week commencing 21 September to protect player welfare.

lead.why: The RFU's decision to postpone the entire English community rugby season due to severe drought is the day's most significant and high-salience story.

teams.heading: Irish rugby watch closely as landmark concussion lawsuit faces potential dismissal
teams.body: The landmark concussion lawsuit against rugby's governing bodies is at risk of being dismissed after a major lawyer change. The legal action, which involves former players seeking damages for brain injuries, has been thrown into jeopardy after a key solicitor quit. Claimants are now seeking new legal representation to keep the case alive. With the high-profile proceedings under threat of collapse, Irish rugby continues to monitor the development as the sport grapples with the long-term safety and welfare of its retired athletes.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy appoints Alex Davies as the new Wales kicking coach
teams.body: Head coach Steve Tandy has added former Leicester coach Alex Davies to his backroom staff ahead of the autumn internationals. Davies, who officially starts next month, will work with the senior squad during Test windows and support age-grade development. He fills the void left by Leigh Halfpenny and Rhys Patchell, who previously held temporary roles. Tandy welcomed his new recruit, saying: "It's great to have Alex join the coaching team. He's a very talented coach who will be another asset for us as a group."

teams.heading: Dave Rennie recalls Will Jordan and Cam Roigard for Ellis Park opener
teams.body: Dave Rennie has handed the All Blacks a significant fitness boost, naming Will Jordan, Cam Roigard and Damian McKenzie to start Saturday’s tour opener at Ellis Park. Jordan and Roigard make their first appearances of the trip after overcoming injury, while McKenzie starts at full-back following an ankle scare. In the second row, Fabian Holland earns a start alongside Josh Lord, with Rennie preferring the youngster’s mobility over Patrick Tuipulotu’s power for the first of three Tests against the world champions.
